chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Yahya ibn al-Mubarik from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a slave who married a free woman, he said: 'The child belongs to the free woman.' And regarding a free man who married a slave woman, he said: 'The child belongs to the father.' As for that which indicates that if it was stipulated that the child should be a slave, then it is so, is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of children born from marriages between slaves and free persons in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the default rules of lineage (walad) in mixed-status marriages, establishing that a child of a slave man and free woman inherits the mother's freedom, while a child of a free man and slave woman inherits the father's enslavement. This ruling underscores the principle that the child follows the status of the parent with the higher social standing in the first case, and the father in the second, reflecting the patriarchal structure of inheritance and manumission. The mention of 'stipulation' (shart) indicates that these defaults can be modified by specific contractual conditions agreed upon at the time of marriage, a nuance important in Shia fiqh regarding the flexibility of marital contracts.
